Marevan (warfarin) is a classic oral [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] used in the treatment of [[atrieflimren]] in Denmark. Within the Danish healthcare quality monitoring system, specifically the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] database (AFDK), Marevan is frequently evaluated and compared against Direct Oral Anticoagulants ([[doac|DOAC]]) to assess treatment safety and efficacy. The primary focus of these comparisons is the incidence of severe adverse events, such as [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]], [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]], and [[iskaemisk-apopleksi|Iskæmisk apopleksi]], among [[praevalente-patienter-med-atrieflimren|Prævalente patienter med atrieflimren]].

Historically, Marevan has been associated with a higher risk of complicated bleeding events compared to newer alternatives. Reports indicate that the risk of intracranial bleeding is expected to decrease over time due to the introduction and widespread adoption of DOACs, which carry a lower risk profile for this specific complication compared to Marevan [^src2]. In the 2023 AFDK annual report, the proportion of patients experiencing intracranial bleeding was recorded at 0.46% for those on Marevan, compared to 0.52% for DOAC [^src1], while severe bleeding occurred in 2.44% of Marevan patients versus 2.33% of DOAC patients [^src3]. Furthermore, among patients not receiving either DOAC or Marevan, the rate of ischemic stroke was 0.53% [^src4].

Subsequent annual reports continue to track these pharmacovigilance and clinical outcomes closely as part of standard [[atrieflimren-behandling]]. In the 2024 report, the incidence of ischemic stroke was 0.51% for Marevan and 0.89% for DOAC [^src7], while intracranial bleeding was reported at 0.82% for Marevan [^src8] and severe bleeding at 2.38% for Marevan compared to 2.30% for DOAC [^src9]. By the 2025 reporting period, the data showed an ischemic stroke rate of 0.88% for Marevan [^src12], an intracranial bleeding rate of 0.63% [^src13], and a severe bleeding rate of 2.54% for Marevan alone, rising to 4.68% for patients concurrently prescribed both DOAC and Marevan [^src14] [^src16]. Detailed clinical outcome analyses from the 2025 report noted that out of 5,043 prevalent patients on Marevan, 45 (0.88%) developed an ischemic stroke [^src15], and out of 5,056 patients on Marevan, 32 (0.63%) experienced an intracranial bleed [^src15]. These metrics are central to national quality indicators, such as [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], and [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], which guide clinical practice and policy decisions regarding anticoagulation in the Danish healthcare system.
